exhibits.punchline: Verdict: void, right. The clause is about automatic debit; the quote is the rule on post-dated cheques, and it drops 'nor a tenancy agreement'.
exhibits.reason: The clause makes pre-authorized debit a mandatory way of paying rent, and a landlord cannot require a particular automatic payment method; a tenant may only choose it voluntarily. clauses.text: No dogs, cats, birds or other animals of any kind may be kept in the rental unit or anywhere in the building.
clauses.label: void
clauses.quote: A provision in a tenancy agreement prohibiting the presence of animals in or about the residential complex is void.
clauses.rationale: A term prohibiting animals in or about the complex is void.

clauses.text: Out of consideration for neighbours with allergies, the Tenant agrees not to keep any animal in the unit.
clauses.label: void
clauses.quote: A provision in a tenancy agreement prohibiting the presence of animals in or about the residential complex is void.
clauses.rationale: A polite reason doesn't change what the term does: it prohibits animals in the unit.

clauses.text: Dogs must be kept on a leash in the lobby, hallways and elevators, and the Tenant shall clean up after any animal in the common areas.
clauses.label: allowed
clauses.quote: A provision in a tenancy agreement prohibiting the presence of animals in or about the residential complex is void.
clauses.rationale: Regulates animals in common areas without prohibiting their presence.

clauses.text: The Tenant shall not allow any animal kept in the unit to damage the unit or to disturb other residents.
clauses.label: allowed
clauses.quote: A provision in a tenancy agreement prohibiting the presence of animals in or about the residential complex is void.
clauses.rationale: Regulates how animals are kept without prohibiting their presence.

clauses.text: If any instalment of rent is not paid when due, the rent for the remainder of the term shall at once become due and payable.
clauses.label: void
clauses.quote: A provision in a tenancy agreement providing that all or part of the remaining rent for a term or period of a tenancy or a specific sum becomes due upon a default of the tenant in paying rent due or in carrying out an obligation is void.
clauses.rationale: Makes the remaining rent fall due on a default in paying rent: an acceleration clause.

clauses.text: The Tenant accepts the unit in its present condition. The Landlord is under no obligation to make any repairs to the unit during the tenancy.
clauses.label: void
clauses.quote: A landlord is responsible for providing and maintaining a residential complex, including the rental units in it, in a good state of repair and fit for habitation
clauses.rationale: Contradicts the landlord's duty to keep the unit in a good state of repair.

clauses.text: The Tenant viewed the unit before signing and is satisfied with its condition. The Tenant will not ask the Landlord to repair any defect that was visible at the viewing.
clauses.label: void
clauses.quote: Subsection (1) applies even if the tenant was aware of a state of non-repair or a contravention of a standard before entering into the tenancy agreement.
clauses.rationale: The repair duty applies even to defects the tenant knew about before signing.

clauses.text: The Tenant shall pay for every repair to the unit during the tenancy, whatever the cause.
clauses.label: void
clauses.quote: A landlord is responsible for providing and maintaining a residential complex, including the rental units in it, in a good state of repair and fit for habitation
clauses.rationale: Shifts the landlord's repair duty to the tenant; the tenant answers only for undue damage caused wilfully or negligently (s. 34).

clauses.text: If there is a fire, a flood, a burst pipe or another emergency in the unit, the Landlord may enter without notice.
clauses.label: allowed
clauses.quote: A landlord may enter a rental unit at any time without written notice, (a) in cases of emergency
clauses.rationale: Entry without written notice is permitted in an emergency.

clauses.text: The Landlord will clean the unit every second Friday and may enter without written notice between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. on those days for that purpose.
clauses.label: allowed
clauses.quote: A landlord may enter a rental unit without written notice to clean it if the tenancy agreement requires the landlord to clean the rental unit at regular intervals and, (a) the landlord enters the unit at the times specified in the tenancy agreement
clauses.rationale: The agreement requires cleaning at regular intervals and entry is at the times it sets.

clauses.text: By signing this Agreement, the Tenant consents to the Landlord entering the unit at any reasonable time without notice.
clauses.label: void
clauses.quote: A landlord may enter a rental unit at any time without written notice, (a) in cases of emergency; or (b) if the tenant consents to the entry at the time of entry.
clauses.rationale: Consent counts only if given at the time of entry; consent given in advance at signing does not replace written notice.

clauses.rationale: The notice must give a time of entry, between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.; this gives only a 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. window.

clauses.rationale: The tenant is responsible for undue damage caused wilfully or negligently by them, an occupant or a guest.

clauses.text: If the Tenant's dog causes undue damage to the floors or doors because the Tenant was careless, the Tenant must pay to repair that damage.
clauses.label: allowed
clauses.quote: The tenant is responsible for the repair of undue damage to the rental unit or residential complex caused by the wilful or negligent conduct of the tenant
clauses.rationale: Damage caused by the tenant's negligence is the tenant's to repair; the term doesn't ban pets.

clauses.quote: The only security deposit that a landlord may collect is a rent deposit collected in accordance with section 106.

clauses.rationale: Exceeds the cap of one rent period or one month's rent, whichever is less.

clauses.rationale: The rent deposit must be applied to the rent for the last rent period.

The clause is generally enforceable as a term of the tenancy, but a landlord cannot use it against a service animal or a disability-related support animal.

The Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (RTA) does not give tenants a right to keep pets, and it does not address pet ownership. Under section 14(1), a tenancy agreement provision is void only to the extent it contravenes the Act, for example by waiving a tenant right under the Act or altering a landlord or tenant obligation the Act imposes. A no-pets clause does neither, so it does not conflict with the RTA.

The main limit comes from outside the RTA. The Ontario *Human Rights Code* (ss. 2 and 3, accommodation) protects tenants with disabilities who need a service animal or an assistance animal. A landlord generally must accommodate that need to the point of undue hardship, and a blanket ban cannot override it. The Landlord and Tenant Board applies the Code in these disputes, so the clause would be unenforceable against such a tenant. The RTA itself is not the source of that limit.

The clause's breadth ("animals of any kind," "anywhere in the building") does not change the analysis under the RTA. It would be read as an ordinary contractual restriction.

The clause is generally enforceable under the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* (RTA). The RTA does not prohibit a landlord and tenant from agreeing to a no-animals term. Section 14(1) makes a tenancy agreement provision void only to the extent that it contravenes the Act or the regulations, purports to waive a right under the Act, or is otherwise inconsistent with it. A general pet ban does none of these things, so it is not void under the RTA.

The clause's stated purpose, consideration for neighbours with allergies, does not affect its validity under the RTA. The tenant's agreement is still a valid term.

Two limits apply, though neither comes from the RTA:

- **Human Rights Code:** Under the *Human Rights Code*, a landlord must accommodate tenants with disabilities to the point of undue hardship. A no-animals clause cannot bar a service animal or an assistance animal needed because of a disability, and it may be unenforceable as applied to such an animal.
- **Enforcement:** A landlord cannot evict for breach of the clause without following the RTA's eviction process through the Landlord and Tenant Board.

The clause is likely **enforceable**. Under the RTA, a tenancy agreement term is void only to the extent it contravenes the Act. Section 14(1) makes provisions that purport to alter the Act's effect void, and this clause does not do that. Nothing in the Act prohibits a landlord from requiring dogs to be leashed in shared areas or tenants to clean up after their animals there. Those are reasonable terms for the use of common property, and they don't limit any right the Act gives the tenant, such as the right to reasonable enjoyment of the unit under s. 22. The clause would become problematic only if it restricted the tenant's use of the rental unit itself in a way the Act forbids, or if it were applied in a way that amounted to harassment or interference.

Under the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* (RTA), rent increases in an ordinary private residential tenancy are governed by Part VII. 

Section 114(1) of the RTA provides that a landlord may increase the rent charged for a rental unit in accordance with Part VII. The specific statutory requirements of Part VII are:
* **Notice:** At least 90 days' written notice in the approved Landlord and Tenant Board form (Section 116(1)).
* **Frequency:** No more than once in any 12-month period (Section 119(1)).
* **Amount:** Capped at the annual rent increase guideline unless an above-guideline increase is authorized (Section 120(1)).

Because the clause strictly restates and complies with these statutory requirements without contracting out of or violating the Act, it is valid and enforceable.

Section 27(1) of the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* allows a landlord to enter a rental unit without written notice where the tenant consents to the entry at the time of entry. A signed blank cheque fits that definition. It is a negotiable instrument, which is property or a right. - **s. 134:** Additional charges are prohibited.

Section 105 is the provision that decides the question.
